correctness.rationale: In an n-vertex nonnegative weighted directed unit-anchored FJ model, varying only edge a->b adds rank-one matrix t e_a(e_a-e_b)^T to I+L(0). Since the latter is a nonsingular M-matrix, H>=0 and x=H e_a has its unique positive maximum at a, implying d=x_a-x_b>0. Sherman-Morrison yields common increasing u=t/(1+dt) and each reduction score s_j sum_i [(I+L(t))^-1]_{ij}/n affine in u. Every strict winning affine score can win on at most one interval, bounding genuine strict switches by n-1. The constructed directed acyclic network with m=n-2 leaves has distinct, strictly increasing slopes and positive strictly ordered adjacent crossing abscissae T_0/2,T_0,...,T_{m-2},T_*; the adjacent crossing weighted-average property forces all n lines onto the upper envelope in turn. Delta, kappa and all opinions satisfy (0,1] rational bounds. Independently checked exact-rational arithmetic for all m=2..18 and direct matrix inverse at n=4,5; n=4 transitions 153/4,153/2,90156. Finite examples complement but do not prove the universal all-n assertion.
residual_risks: Nonnegative fixed edge structure, one varied edge and strict winner convention are essential.
One edge varying monotonically is crucial to the common fractional-linear parameter.

value.rationale: The exact number of optimum intervention reversals is a natural parameter-sensitivity invariant for network opinion optimization. The nonreturn property is universal and its sharpness is realized by an explicit valid nonnegative network of every size n>=4 with all vertices winning in sequence. This is more informative than a generic line-envelope observation or a fixed-network calculation.
residual_risks: Many switches occur at large weights in constructed examples; theorem does not optimize weight budget or cover multiple interventions.

limitations: One nonnegative edge varies from zero, fixed innate opinions, unit anchoring, strict unique winners; tie breaks alone do not count.
No claim for signed or time-varying edge weights, simultaneous edge changes or multi-seed selection.
